newsitem.title: USA: EntreMed buys back thalidomide rights.
newsitem.headline: EntreMed buys back thalidomide rights.

text.p: EntreMed Inc said Monday it had re-acquired the commercial rights to thalidomide from Bristol-Myers Squibb Co and had extended Bristol's warrant to purchase additional equity in EntreMed.
EntreMed also said it had renewed Bristol's warrant to purchase $10 million of EntreMed stock at $22.50 a share while continuing its evaluation of EntreMed's new antiangiogenic product candidates.
EntreMed stock was trading at 11, up 5/8, Monday afternoon.

"We are pleased to now control the development of thalidomide as it applies to cancer and blindness, which allows us to expand our business development opportunities," John Holaday, EntreMed chairman, president and chief executive officer, said in a press release.
According to EntreMed, Bristol retains rights to thalidomide analogs that are under development as next-generation oral antiangiogenic drugs.

EntreMed said Bristol will continue to fund the ongoing antiangiogenic research and development efforts of EntreMed at the same level as before, but future milestone payments related to thalidomide no longer apply.
